about: Marks a file name carries when it is another version of the same file: a copy number, a version number, an export time, a backup. A name with these marks taken off its end is the name of its family; files in one folder with the same family name and extension are versions of one file. A mark with never_current is only ever on an older copy (a backup made before a change), so a family member without it is shown as the latest when one exists. A mark with orders "number" carries a number in its first group ("v5_3" is 5.3): a member whose number is below another member's is never the latest, whatever time its copy was saved at, because a download or a copy changes the time and not which version it is. A new kind of mark is one row here.

marks.says: a copy number, as in "notes (1)" or "notes (2)"
the word copy, as in "notes copy" or "notes copy 2"
a version number, as in "blocks_v5_7", "plan v2" or "book-V1.1"
a saved time in brackets, as in "README(20260905-215248)"
a backup made before a change, as in "steward.backup-before-reconciliation-20260901T142317Z" or "steward.pre-correction-20260831T1949"
